title: Do Neem (The Split)
content:
​Duniya ne sikhaya ki aurat ko batna padta hai,

Apni hi rooh ke do hisse karke jeena padta hai.

She was told She must divide her life in two,

To pick which half of her gets to survive.

Ya toh naram hawayein chuno, jinme zindagi ki barish na ho,

Ya sang-e-marmar ki aisi chhat, jahan dhadkan ki gunjaish na ho.

To choose a gentle hand that has no path,

Or a sturdy roof where no love can thrive.

​With one, the night was warm, the words were soft,

​Ek shakhs mila, jiske lafz shabnam aur raatein makhmal thi,

Usne maathe ki shikan toh choom li, par sehar ka bojh mujh par chhod diya.

Usne haath toh thama, par zindagi ki gadi mujh par chhod di,

Uske be-fikr aangan ko roshan rakhne ki khatir, maine apne wajood ko jala diya.

He held my heart, but left my hands to build.

I carried all the weight, the bills, the home,

Until the warmth we had was slowly chilled.

​Doosra woh tha, jiske sange-marmar mahal ki deewarein Unchi thi,

Duniya ne uske rutbe aur sone ke darwazon par salam kiya.

Par us aali-shaan thikane mein, meri rooh barf mein tabdeel ho gayi,

Usne aasaish toh di, par meri befikre masoomiyat ko dafan kar diya.

Woh rishta nahi, dilon ka nahi, bas ek kaagzi sauda sa tha,

Aur main us sangemarmar ke qile mein, ek sangemarmar ki malka thi.

With the other, all on the papers looked so right,

A house of stone, a title, and a name.

But inside those walls, the air grew ice,

And my gentle free spirit was bound inside.

​Zamana kehta hai, aaj ki kaabil aurat ka yahi naseeb hai

Ya mohabbat ke badle apna khoon-paseena girwi rakh de,

ya hifazat ke badle apne jazbaat.

Aur main in aade-adhure paimanon ke beech ghutti rahi,

Ek jahan jo muqammal hone ki zid karta tha, is fareb mein tadapta rahi.

They said: “A woman cannot have it all—

Settle for a lover, or settle for a cage.”

And so I suffocated in the split,

Trapped between the warmth and the page.

​Par ab, kisi khokhli neev par mera aashiyana nahi banega,

Kisi thande saaye ko garmi dene ke liye, mera aansoo nahi jalega.

Na main bojh uthaungi, na kisi pinjre mein saans rok kar baithungi,

Maine aadhe aasmaan se samjhauta karna chhod diya hai.

​Mujhe mazboot chhat k sath thikana bhi chahiye, aur sardi ki dhoop si narmi bhi,

Jo ishq aurat ko tod de, bahaane banaye, woh meri manzil nahi.

Ab yeh safar aakhiri sach ki taraf mudega

Ya toh muqammal milega, ya yeh ladki khud apni mehboob rahegi.

It looked so right,
A house of stone, a title, and a name.
But inside those walls, the air grew ice,
And my gentle free spirit was bound inside.

The world says this is the fate of today’s capable woman:
She must either mortgage her blood and sweat in exchange for love,
Or mortgage her emotions in exchange for safety.
And I suffocated between these half-baked standards,
Agonizing in the delusion of a world that insisted on calling itself complete.

They said: “A woman cannot have it all—
Settle for a lover, or settle for a cage.”
And so I suffocated in the split,
Trapped between the warmth and the page.

But now, my nest will not be built on a hollow foundation,
Nor will my tears burn to warm a cold shadow.
I will neither carry the burden nor sit breathless in a cage,
I have stopped compromising for half a sky.

I need a home with a sturdy roof, but also the softness of winter sunshine,
The love that breaks a woman and makes excuses is not my destination.
Now this journey will turn toward the ultimate truth—
Either I will get what is complete, or this girl will remain her own beloved.
